Random sampling counters automation bias by ensuring that not all investigations are based solely on high-risk signals generated by algorithms. By incorporating a random sample into the fraud detection process, inspectors are encouraged to critically evaluate cases rather than relying blindly on algorithmic results. This approach helps to monitor and mitigate risks of discrimination, as it allows for a more balanced selection of cases for investigation.

Regarding the AI Act duties for high-risk providers, the use of random sampling aligns with the requirements for high-risk AI systems to identify and mitigate reasonably foreseeable risks, including potential discrimination. The AI Act mandates that providers of high-risk systems must implement measures to ensure compliance with these obligations, and random sampling can serve as a control tool to help fulfill these duties by providing a mechanism to assess and improve the fairness and effectiveness of the algorithms used.
